feed.title: Science & Academia — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: earth nullschool
entry.content:
Visualisation of global wind, ocean-current and air-pollution forecasts on a live globe. Unlike weather apps, it shows surface and atmosphere layers at planetary scale rather than a local forecast.

https://earth.nullschool.net

entry.title: OpenAlex
entry.content:
An open catalogue of scholarly works, authors, institutions and journals; all the data is CC0 and queryable through a free API. Unlike Semantic Scholar the data can be reused without restriction; it was set up to replace the Microsoft Academic Graph when that shut down.

https://openalex.org/

entry.title: TOP500
entry.content:
The twice-yearly ranking of the 500 fastest supercomputers by LINPACK results, with all past lists. Unlike general hardware news it offers decades of comparable measurements.

https://www.top500.org/

entry.title: Türkiye Bursları
entry.content:
Turkey’s government scholarship programme for international students at bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral level; coverage, programmes and the application calendar live here. Unlike a single university’s scholarship it bundles tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation and a year of Turkish language study in one application.

https://www.turkiyeburslari.gov.tr/

entry.title: YÖK Atlas
entry.content:
Placement data for Turkish undergraduate and associate programmes: base scores and ranks, quotas, which provinces and high schools students come from, the academic staff. Unlike prep-school ranking lists it is official, programme-level data built on ÖSYM placements.

https://yokatlas.yok.gov.tr/

entry.title: YÖK Yükseköğretim İstatistikleri
entry.content:
Statistics from the Council of Higher Education’s information system: student and academic-staff counts by university, faculty and programme. Unlike YÖK Atlas it is not admissions data but headcount tables across the whole system.

https://istatistik.yok.gov.tr/

entry.title: Zotero
entry.content:
An open-source reference manager: its browser connector saves the citation and PDF from an article page in one click, and the Word and LibreOffice plugins format citations and bibliographies in thousands of styles. Unlike publisher-owned managers such as Mendeley it is developed by a non-profit; only cloud storage beyond a small quota is paid.

https://www.zotero.org/

entry.title: Awesome Agriculture
entry.content:
A list of open-source technology and tools for farming and gardening. Unlike commercial agriculture software, it gathers only open-source options — sensors, irrigation, farm management, data.

https://github.com/brycejohnston/awesome-agriculture

entry.title: Awesome Bioinformatics
entry.content:
A list of tools and resources for analysing biological data (bioinformatics). Unlike general data-science lists, it focuses on biology-specific tools such as sequence alignment and variant calling.

https://github.com/danielecook/Awesome-Bioinformatics

entry.title: Awesome Citizen Science
entry.content:
A list for community-based, non-institutional science (citizen science). Unlike academic science resources, it gathers projects, tools and hardware open to people outside institutions.

https://github.com/dylanrees/citizen-science

entry.title: Awesome Clean Tech
entry.content:
A list of projects and resources fighting climate change with technology. Unlike general sustainability writing, it focuses on open-source projects and areas where developers can contribute.

https://github.com/nglgzz/awesome-clean-tech

entry.title: Awesome Computational Biology
entry.content:
A list of resources for computational approaches to biology problems. Unlike tool-heavy bioinformatics lists, it pairs courses, books and methods with the tools.

https://github.com/inoue0426/awesome-computational-biology

entry.title: Awesome Healthcare
entry.content:
A list of open-source healthcare software for facilities. Unlike commercial health software, it gathers open-source options — electronic health records, imaging, standards such as HL7/FHIR.

https://github.com/kakoni/awesome-healthcare

entry.title: Awesome Information Retrieval
entry.content:
A list of information-retrieval resources for learning to build your own search engine. Unlike the docs of ready engines such as Elasticsearch, it teaches the theory underneath — indexing, ranking, evaluation.

https://github.com/harpribot/awesome-information-retrieval

entry.title: Awesome LaTeX
entry.content:
A list of packages, templates and tools for LaTeX, the scientific typesetting language. Unlike Overleaf’s docs, it gathers editors, packages and templates without tying them to one service.

https://github.com/egeerardyn/awesome-LaTeX

entry.title: Awesome Neuroimaging
entry.content:
A list of imaging software for analysing brain data from living subjects. Unlike general image-processing lists, it focuses on software specific to brain data such as MRI and fMRI.

https://github.com/NPACore/awesome-neuroimaging

entry.title: Awesome Neuroscience
entry.content:
A list of computational resources for studying the nervous system and brain. Unlike the neuroimaging list, it focuses on computational modelling, data sources and courses rather than imaging.

https://github.com/analyticalmonk/awesome-neuroscience

entry.title: Awesome Quarto
entry.content:
A resource list for Quarto, the scientific and technical open-source publishing system. Unlike R Markdown it is language-agnostic: you write the same document with Python, R, Julia or Observable.

https://github.com/mcanouil/awesome-quarto

entry.title: Awesome Scientific Computing
entry.content:
A list of tools and libraries for solving complex scientific problems by computer. Unlike data-science lists, it focuses on numerical methods — finite elements, linear algebra, differential-equation solvers.

https://github.com/nschloe/awesome-scientific-computing

entry.title: Awesome Theoretical CS
entry.content:
A list for the interplay of computer science and pure mathematics (theoretical CS). Unlike practical programming lists, it covers theoretical fields such as complexity theory, algorithm analysis and logic.

https://github.com/mostafatouny/awesome-theoretical-computer-science

entry.title: Begin LaTeX in Minutes
entry.content:
A brief intro to LaTeX for beginners, in minutes. Unlike Overleaf’s long guides it is a one-page quick start: document structure, maths, tables and bibliography basics. The repository is archived (last update November 2020); LaTeX basics have not changed, so it still reads fine.

https://github.com/LewisVo/Begin-Latex-in-minutes

entry.title: DBLP
entry.content:
The open bibliography database of computer science publications, with tidy author pages and conference volumes. Against Google Scholar it is clean and hand-maintained — author ambiguity and phantom records are rare.

https://dblp.org/

entry.title: Computer History Museum
entry.content:
Oral history interviews with the pioneers of computing, plus a lecture archive. Unlike technical channels it records the circumstances a decision was made in — the context no document holds.

https://www.youtube.com/user/ComputerHistory/videos

entry.title: Nature
entry.content:
One of science’s most prestigious peer-reviewed journals, carrying news and research together. Unlike preprint archives its strict peer review gives published findings their weight.

https://www.nature.com/

entry.title: OpenStax
entry.content:
A Rice University project offering university textbooks free and openly licensed. Unlike commercial texts it gives full, peer-reviewed volumes that are free and regularly updated.

https://openstax.org/

entry.title: PhET Simulations
entry.content:
The University of Colorado’s interactive simulations for physics, chemistry and maths. Unlike a lecture it lets you experience a concept by tweaking its parameters by hand.

https://phet.colorado.edu/

entry.title: Semantic Scholar
entry.content:
An AI-powered academic search engine. Unlike Google Scholar it summarises a paper, distinguishes influential citations and extracts links semantically.

https://www.semanticscholar.org/

entry.title: Connected Papers
entry.content:
A tool that starts from one paper and builds a visual graph of related work. Unlike a citation list it draws a “map” of a field and shows neighbouring work.

https://www.connectedpapers.com/

entry.title: SKYbrary
entry.content:
An EUROCONTROL-backed aviation safety knowledge base of accident analyses, human factors and safety management systems. Unlike general aviation sites it focuses on safety — a usable archive for anyone thinking about high-reliability system design.

https://skybrary.aero/

entry.title: İÜ Gazete Arşivi
entry.content:
Istanbul University’s scanned historical newspaper collection. Unlike secondary literature it is a primary source, where the details that literature skips turn up.

https://nek.istanbul.edu.tr/ekos/GAZETE/

entry.title: Nişanyan Yeradları
entry.content:
A historical inventory of settlement names in and around Turkey. Unlike official place-name lists, it documents former names and every change with date and source — nothing else compiles this systematically.

https://www.nisanyanyeradlari.com/

entry.title: David Rumsey Harita Koleksiyonu
entry.content:
A high-resolution historical map archive. Unlike plain scanned collections, it lets you georeference maps onto modern geography — a strong tool for tracking place-name and border change.

https://www.davidrumsey.com/

entry.title: Transkribus · Osmanlıca
entry.content:
A text-recognition model trained on printed Ottoman Turkish. Unlike general OCR tools it can read Arabic-script Turkish — a gap that is critical in archive research.

https://www.transkribus.org/models/ottoman-turkish-print#tryit

entry.title: ABD Antarktika Programı
entry.content:
The official portal of the US Antarctic research programme, with material on field logistics and station operations. Unlike general science news, it details how systems are operated in extreme conditions.

https://www.usap.gov/

entry.title: Devlet Arşivleri
entry.content:
Turkey’s official archive institution and the gateway to catalogues and digital copies of Ottoman and Republican-era documents. Unlike secondary sources, it takes you to the original document.

https://www.devletarsivleri.gov.tr/

entry.title: Aperta
entry.content:
TÜBİTAK’s open archive, hosting research data alongside publications. Data sharing is not yet common in Turkey, which makes it notable.

https://aperta.ulakbim.gov.tr/

entry.title: Harman
entry.content:
A harvester searching Turkey’s institutional academic archives from one place. Instead of hunting for theses and articles university by university, one search covers them all.

https://harman.ulakbim.gov.tr/index

entry.title: DergiPark
entry.content:
The open-access platform for Turkish academic journals, hosting over a thousand titles — the primary source for Turkish literature, not aggregated anywhere else.

https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/

entry.title: Wolfram Alpha
entry.content:
A computational knowledge engine that integrates, converts units and compares data. Unlike a search engine it computes the answer rather than finding it, showing the working step by step in the paid tier.

https://www.wolframalpha.com/

entry.title: iNaturalist
entry.content:
Share nature observations and get species identified. Unlike species-ID apps it has community verification: confirmed records become research-grade and flow into GBIF — a rare case of a hobby producing real data.

https://www.inaturalist.org/
